data.one_liner: Portable file system API working identically on io, web (IndexedDB/OPFS) and memory.
data.what_it_does: Provides an asynchronous subset of dart:io File, Directory, and Link behind a FileSystem abstraction. Enables identical file system code to run on native IO, browser storage, and in-memory for testing.
use_when: You need file system operations that work on both Flutter mobile/desktop and web browsers.
You want to unit test file-dependent code easily using an in-memory file system.
avoid_when: You require synchronous file I/O (browser storage is strictly asynchronous).
You need advanced OS features not mapped in dart:io (e.g., watching file changes or process execution).
strengths: Consistent asynchronous API across IO, web (IndexedDB and OPFS), and memory.
Great for writing testable code with in-memory files.
Drop-in wrapper or replacement for dart:io file classes via fs_io.dart.
weaknesses: Asynchronous API only; no synchronous methods are available.
OPFS backend does not support links or random access.
Web storage is bound by browser quotas.

alternatives.name: file
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need a pluggable file system abstraction for dart:io without web (IndexedDB/OPFS) or memory-specific implementations built in.
